strategy_title: Doubling BLOCK_M and BLOCK_K Causes Shared Memory and Register Pressure Regression
strategy_description: Increasing BLOCK_M from 64→128 and BLOCK_K from 32→64 in a small GEMM kernel (M=7840, N=32, K=192) caused a 26% slowdown despite reducing per-instruction warp stall cycles (7.99→5.73). The larger tiles tripled dynamic shared memory per block (24.58→81.92 KB), collapsing the shared-memory block limit from 6 to 2 blocks/SM and cutting theoretical occupancy from 37.5% to 12.5%. Simultaneously, register count jumped from 80 to 114 per thread, further constraining occupancy. The instruction count nearly doubled (1.99M→3.71M) because the larger tiles did more work per block but the grid shrank, leaving more SMs idle. The net effect was a 35% longer kernel duration despite slightly better per-instruction efficiency.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: smaller tiles, lower register/smem pressure
BLOCK_M = 64
BLOCK_N = 32
BLOCK_K = 32
# dynamic_smem = 24.58 KB/block → 6 blocks/SM possible
# registers = 80/thread
# theoretical occupancy = 37.5%
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (actually slower): larger tiles, higher register/smem pressure
BLOCK_M = 128
BLOCK_N = 32
BLOCK_K = 64
# dynamic_smem = 81.92 KB/block → only 2 blocks/SM possible
# registers = 114/thread
# theoretical occupancy = 12.5%
# instruction count ~2x higher, duration 35% longer
applicable_when: Never apply this specific tile size increase (BLOCK_M 64→128, BLOCK_K 32→64) when the kernel already has low achieved occupancy (~6%) and the shared memory per block is already near the SM limit. The shared memory block limit is the binding constraint.
do_not_apply_when: Do not increase BLOCK_M or BLOCK_K when dynamic shared memory per block is already ≥20 KB and the shared-memory block limit (Block Limit Shared Mem) is ≤6. Tripling shared memory per block will collapse the block limit from 6→2, cutting theoretical occupancy by 3x and causing regression even if per-instruction stall cycles improve. Also avoid when register count is already high (≥80/thread), as larger tiles push register pressure further and compound the occupancy loss.
framework_notes: In Triton, BLOCK_M and BLOCK_K are constexpr tile parameters that directly determine shared memory allocation size (proportional to BLOCK_M*BLOCK_K*dtype_bytes). Increasing these parameters increases both register pressure (compiler spills more) and shared memory footprint, both of which reduce SM occupancy. The Block Limit Shared Mem metric in NCU directly shows how many blocks can co-reside per SM given the shared memory allocation.

strategy_title: Reduce num_warps + Add num_stages to Hide SMEM Stalls
strategy_description: When a kernel is dominated by MIO/shared-memory scoreboard stalls (CPIStall MIO fraction >70%, Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction ~8, scheduler No Eligible >87%), reducing num_warps (e.g. 4→2, halving block size from 128→64 threads) combined with adding pipeline stages (num_stages=2 or 3 via @triton.autotune) can significantly reduce kernel duration. In this case, the change cut Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction from 8.07 to 3.13 (61% reduction) and duration from 23.71µs to 18.05µs (1.32x speedup), while the scheduler No Eligible dropped from 87.56% to 68.06%. The mechanism is twofold: fewer warps per block reduces register pressure enough to relax the register block limit (6→8 blocks/SM), and pipeline stages enable async prefetching of the next tile to overlap compute with shared memory latency, even when bank conflicts persist.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: no autotune, fixed num_warps=4 (block_size=128), no pipelining
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    # 80 registers/thread, 6 blocks/SM (register-limited)
    # Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction = 8.07
    # Scheduler No Eligible = 87.56%
    # Duration = 23.71us
applicable_when: Kernel shows CPIStall MIO fraction >60%, Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction >6, Scheduler No Eligible >80%, and SharedMemoryConflicts with >15-way average bank conflicts. The kernel is a small GEMM or similar tiled computation where tile sizes (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) are already near-optimal and cannot be changed without SMEM/register regression. The register block limit and SMEM block limit are both binding (~6 blocks/SM).
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply when the kernel already has high achieved occupancy (>20%) or when the grid is large enough to fully saturate all SMs (waves_per_sm >1). Also avoid when increasing num_stages would push dynamic SMEM per block beyond the SM shared memory limit, collapsing the SMEM block limit below 2. Note that this approach does not eliminate bank conflicts (they persist at 13.2-way after optimization) — if conflict elimination is possible via padding or access reordering, that should be preferred.
framework_notes: In Triton, num_warps controls threads per block (num_warps * 32 = block_size). Reducing num_warps from 4 to 2 halves block_size from 128 to 64, which can relax the register block limit (Block Limit Registers in NCU) since fewer threads share the SM register file. num_stages in Triton enables async double/triple-buffering of SMEM tiles on Hopper (wgmma-style pipeline), allocating num_stages copies of the A and B tiles in shared memory. The autotune key=[] means the best config is selected once globally (not per problem size), which is appropriate when M/N/K are fixed constants in the kernel.

strategy_title: Autotune num_warps to Halve Shared Memory Bank Conflicts
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with configs sweeping num_warps={2,4} and num_stages={2,3} selected a 2-warp (64-thread) block configuration, which halved the block size from 128 to 64 threads. This reduced dynamic shared memory per block from 24.58 KB to 12.29 KB, allowing up to 10 blocks/SM instead of 6, and cut warp cycles per issued instruction from 8.07 to 3.72 (2.2x improvement). The SharedMemoryConflicts bank conflict way-count dropped from 17.9-way to 13.2-way, and the scheduler eligible-warp percentage more than doubled (12.4% → 27.3%), indicating substantially better latency hiding. The net effect was a 12.7% reduction in kernel duration despite higher registers per thread (80→96) and lower achieved occupancy (6.24%→3.12%), because the smaller block size reduced the shared memory footprint enough to relieve the binding shared-memory block limit constraint.
slow_pseudocode:
# No autotune — fixed block_size=128 (num_warps=4)
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    # dynamic_smem = 24.58 KB/block → Block Limit Shared Mem = 6
    # Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction = 8.07
    # Scheduler No Eligible = 87.56%
    # SharedMemoryConflicts: 17.9-way, 72.68% speedup potential
applicable_when: Kernel has high SharedMemoryConflicts (>10-way bank conflicts, >60% of wavefronts are conflicts) AND the shared memory block limit (Block Limit Shared Mem) is the binding occupancy constraint AND the kernel uses a fixed block size without autotuning. Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction > 6 and Scheduler No Eligible > 80% are strong indicators. The shared memory allocation must scale with block size (i.e., reducing num_warps reduces smem per block).
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply when the kernel's shared memory allocation is independent of block size (e.g., fixed-size smem buffers). Also avoid when achieved occupancy is already high (>20%) or when the grid is already much larger than SM count (waves_per_sm > 1), as the autotuner overhead may not be worth it. If Block Limit Shared Mem is not the binding constraint (e.g., register limit is lower), reducing block size will not help the smem bottleneck.
framework_notes: In Triton, num_warps controls block size (block_size = num_warps * 32). Shared memory allocated via tl.make_block_ptr or explicit smem buffers that scale with BLOCK_M/BLOCK_K tile sizes will shrink proportionally when num_warps is reduced. The @triton.autotune decorator with key=[] means the autotuner runs once and caches the best config for all inputs — appropriate when problem dimensions are fixed. num_stages controls software pipelining depth and affects register pressure.

strategy_title: Autotune num_stages and num_warps to hide MIO stall latency
strategy_description: When a Triton GEMM kernel shows high MIO scoreboard stall fraction (>70% of warp cycles) and very low scheduler eligibility (<15% eligible cycles), adding @triton.autotune over num_stages (1–4) and num_warps (2–4) allows the compiler to select a software pipeline depth that overlaps global-to-shared memory loads with tl.dot compute. In this case, autotune selected a configuration (likely num_warps=2) that halved Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction from 8.07 to 4.04 and reduced Mem Busy from 72.9% to 48%, yielding a 7% speedup. The winning config also halved dynamic shared memory per block (24.58→12.29 KB), suggesting num_warps=2 with a shallower pipeline was chosen, trading theoretical occupancy (37.5%→31.25%) for lower per-instruction stall latency.
slow_pseudocode:
# No autotune — fixed num_warps=4, num_stages=1 (default)
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
        a = tl.load(a_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
        b = tl.load(b_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
        acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False, out_dtype=tl.float32)
        a_block_ptr = tl.advance(a_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
        b_block_ptr = tl.advance(b_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
# block_size=128 (4 warps), Warp Cycles/Inst=8.07, No Eligible=87.56%

# Autotune over num_warps and num_stages
@triton.autotune(
    configs=[
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=1),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=2),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=3),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=4),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=1),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=2),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=3),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=4),
    ],
    key=[],
)
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
        a = tl.load(a_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
        b = tl.load(b_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
        acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False, out_dtype=tl.float32)
        a_block_ptr = tl.advance(a_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
        b_block_ptr = tl.advance(b_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
# Winning config: num_warps=2 (block_size=64), Warp Cycles/Inst=4.04, No Eligible=75.6%
applicable_when: Triton GEMM kernel with: (1) MIO scoreboard stall fraction >60% of warp cycles, (2) scheduler eligibility <20% (No Eligible >80%), (3) fixed num_warps with no autotune, (4) low achieved occupancy (<10%) with only 1 active warp per scheduler. The kernel has a k-loop over tiles where global-to-shared loads dominate latency.
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply when the kernel already has high achieved occupancy (>30%) or when the k-loop has very few iterations (K/BLOCK_K < 3), as the pipeline depth cannot amortize the overhead. Also avoid when register pressure is already near the limit and increasing num_stages would push registers/thread high enough to collapse block limits. Note: this approach may introduce uncoalesced local load/store patterns (new NCU warning after) if the compiler spills registers due to higher register count from autotune.
framework_notes: In Triton, num_stages in @triton.autotune controls the software pipeline depth for the k-loop: num_stages=2 inserts one prefetch stage, num_stages=3 inserts two. On Hopper (H200), Triton may use TMA/cp.async.bulk for the prefetch. num_warps controls block size (num_warps*32 threads). Both are passed implicitly to the JIT compiler — no loop body changes needed. key=[] is valid when all problem dimensions are compile-time constants in the kernel body.

strategy_title: Flipping B smem order + num_warps=1 causes register explosion
strategy_description: Changing the B block pointer's shared memory layout order from (0,1) to (1,0) — intended to coalesce shared memory reads for tl.dot — combined with adding num_warps=1 configs to autotune caused a severe regression (0.74x). The autotune selected num_warps=1 (block_size=32), which caused registers per thread to jump from 128 to 168, cutting theoretical occupancy from 25% to 18.75% and achieved occupancy from 3.12% to 1.56%. Although Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction marginally improved (3.13→2.94) and shared memory bank conflicts reduced (13.2-way→9.5-way), the dominant effect was that the register explosion from num_warps=1 more than doubled kernel duration (18.05µs→32.26µs). The smem order change itself may have forced the compiler to insert a transpose or additional register-resident buffering, inflating register count by 40 registers/thread.
applicable_when: Never apply this combination when the kernel already has high register pressure (>100 registers/thread) and low achieved occupancy (<5%). Adding num_warps=1 to the autotune search space when registers/thread are already high will cause the compiler to allocate even more registers per thread (since fewer threads share the register file budget), collapsing occupancy further.
do_not_apply_when: Do not add num_warps=1 configs to autotune when registers per thread are already ≥100 at num_warps=2. The register count scales inversely with num_warps in Triton — halving warps can increase registers/thread by 30-40%, which at already-high register counts will collapse the register block limit and reduce achieved occupancy below the already-low baseline. Do not change B block pointer smem order (0,1)→(1,0) when the kernel is already achieving good Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction (<4) via pipeline staging — the compiler may insert implicit transposes that inflate register usage.
framework_notes: In Triton, the order parameter of tl.make_block_ptr specifies which dimension is contiguous in shared memory (order=(1,0) means dim-1 is fastest). Changing this order for the B matrix in a GEMM can force the Triton compiler to insert a layout conversion (transpose) in registers before feeding tl.dot, which significantly increases register pressure. On Hopper, tl.dot expects specific wgmma-compatible layouts; mismatched smem order may require extra register-resident buffering. num_warps=1 (32 threads/block) should be avoided when registers/thread are already ≥100, as the compiler allocates more registers per thread to compensate for fewer threads sharing work.
